items.title: Tyner McCoy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I was in the book, some other pianists were in the book, maybe Keith, I’m not sure... I like the fact that whatever he tried to portray, he didn’t limit himself.

ctx.x: Yeah I wanted to ask you about that. Now Billy Taylor, Steinway artist, Ahmad Jamal, Steinway artist. What is it about the Steinway, and talk about your relationship with the Steinway Company.

Well they make one of the greatest pianos in the world. The way it’s constructed, the way it sounds, they really know what they’re doing and they have had years and years of opportunities to perfect the instrument. Steinway is a really great piano and it’s durability, the fact that you can play it for a long time and it will keep it’s tuned. The very terms of preserving the instrument should keep it tuned, otherwise once it gets so flat that the guys got to spend a long time-he can’t pull the strings up and back…

have a book I think Bill was in the book, I was in the book, some other pianists were in the book, maybe Keith, I’m not sure, but they honor artists, they make it Steinway artists. If you're stuck somewhere you can call a guy who has a franchise and he can’t say, “No I’m not going to” because Steinway piano . . . you have a relationship with the company, so it works out some kind of way.
